name: Task Completion Rate
what_it_measures: Fraction of assigned tasks reaching verified goal end-states without fatal exceptions or stalled loops.
how_to_run: Execute curated test scenarios against sandboxed environments or ground-truth state checkers and compute binary pass ratios.
strengths: Directly reflects real end-to-end usefulness rather than surface conversational politeness.
limitations: Hides inefficient thrashing, expensive retries, or unsafe intermediate side effects unless paired with cost and trajectory checks.

name: pass^k Reliability Consistency
what_it_measures: Probability that an agent solves the exact same task across repeated independent runs despite stochastic sampling variance.
how_to_run: Run each test task repeatedly under production sampling settings and track how steeply multi-run success decays relative to single-attempt success.
strengths: Exposes flaky policies that look adequate on optimistic single attempts yet fail unacceptably under enterprise reliability demands.
limitations: Multiplies benchmark execution time and compute costs proportionally to repetition factor.

name: Faithfulness and Groundedness
what_it_measures: Degree to which every factual claim emitted by an agent is directly entailed by retrieved passages or observed tool outputs.
how_to_run: Decompose generated answers into atomic claims and verify each claim against supplied context using NLI models or calibrated judges.
strengths: Measures hallucination leakage cleanly even when external ground-truth answers are unavailable.
limitations: High faithfulness alone does not prove retrieved chunks actually answered the user's original question.

name: Context Precision and Recall
what_it_measures: Whether RAG retrieval pipelines rank relevant source chunks near the top and avoid omitting crucial supporting facts.
how_to_run: Compare retrieved chunks against annotated ground-truth evidence spans or rubric claims across test queries.
strengths: Isolates indexer, chunking, embedding, and reranker quality cleanly from downstream LLM phrasing effects.
limitations: Evaluating retrieval recall requires annotated reference passages or expensive synthetic claim decomposition.

name: Tool Call Schema and Argument Accuracy
what_it_measures: Correctness of model-selected function names, JSON Schema types, required fields, and semantically valid argument values.
how_to_run: Run multi-turn and single-turn prompts with tool definitions and compare parsed tool AST arguments against expected specifications.
strengths: Detects syntax drift, hallucinated parameters, and wrong tool routing rapidly without hitting live external side effects.
limitations: Passing syntactic argument checks does not guarantee downstream multi-step domain outcomes succeed.

name: Trajectory Efficiency and Step Overhead
what_it_measures: Comparison between actual tool invocations, redundant retries, and total tokens consumed versus optimal task paths.
how_to_run: Log tool trace length, duplicate call hashes, and cumulative token counts per run and compare against reference solution baselines.
strengths: Catches invisible prompt bloat and subtle search thrashing before production API bills spike.
limitations: Over-penalizing extra exploratory verification steps can pressure models toward premature ungrounded guesses.

name: Citation Attribution Precision
what_it_measures: Accuracy with which inline source links and footnote snippets genuinely support the claims they accompany.
how_to_run: Audit emitted citation spans programmatically or via human review to verify referenced IDs exist and entail associated claims.
strengths: Prevents fabricated plausible links from eroding user trust in research, legal, and compliance outputs.
limitations: Fine-grained span verification can be slow on heavily synthesized cross-document reports.

name: Adversarial Attack Success Rate
what_it_measures: Proportion of simulated prompt-injection, jailbreak, or data-exfiltration probes that bypass agent guardrails or authorization boundaries.
how_to_run: Execute curated red-team attack suites over direct inputs and untrusted retrieved files and detect forbidden tool calls or leaks.
strengths: Quantifies defensive robustness cleanly across security guardrail revisions and permission boundary updates.
limitations: Zero observed exploits on known test suites cannot certify immunity against novel unseen attack phrasing.

name: Response Latency and Time-to-First-Token
what_it_measures: Interactive responsiveness covering initial token streaming onset alongside full multi-turn completion duration across tool runs.
how_to_run: Record OpenTelemetry span timestamps across network gateways, model completions, retrieval lookups, and tool calls.
strengths: Guides practical caching, routing, and parallel execution tuning aligned with conversational human expectations.
limitations: Raw inference speed metrics ignore whether fast answers were actually accurate or grounded.

name: LLM-as-a-Judge Rubric Grading
what_it_measures: Qualitative scoring methodology applying calibrated evaluator models with explicit rubrics or blind pairwise comparison across candidate runs.
how_to_run: Configure judge prompt templates with explicit grading scales, randomize candidate order on comparisons, and verify calibration against human labels.
strengths: Enables continuous automated assessment on open-ended prose and subtle instruction compliance where exact equality fails.
limitations: Vulnerable to verbosity bias, position preference, and shared model blind spots unless calibrated periodically.

name: RAG Triad Diagnostic Method
what_it_measures: Structured diagnostic decomposition scoring query-context relevance, context-response groundedness, and query-response answer relevance jointly.
how_to_run: Log retrieval context and model output triples per interaction and inspect weakest triad link scores to prioritize engineering fixes.
strengths: Pinpoints whether failures stem from chunking/retrieval gaps or generation hallucination cleanly.
limitations: Assumes answer quality reduces cleanly to retrieved passage fidelity without heavy external action logic.

name: Deterministic State and Unit Verification
what_it_measures: Validating agent effectiveness strictly via objective end-state checks such as database rows, compiled builds, unit tests, and typed schemas.
how_to_run: Execute agent actions inside seeded isolated state snapshots and run prewritten assertion scripts after execution finishes.
strengths: Eliminates subjective grading ambiguity and directly verifies genuine functional correctness.
limitations: Requires engineering dedicated mock fixtures or sandboxed environments for every tested workflow.

name: Simulated User and Policy Interaction Method
what_it_measures: Testing conversational agents against persona-driven LLM user simulators within stateful policy and tool sandboxes.
how_to_run: Provide a user simulator persona and secret objective, run multi-turn dialogues plus tool mutations, and score policy compliance plus end DB state.
strengths: Exposes conversational misunderstanding, multi-turn drift, and sycophancy flaws unreachable via static single prompts.
limitations: Simulated users may behave more coherently or cleanly than unpredictable frustrated human callers.

name: Blind Human Expert Calibration
what_it_measures: Structured domain expert review of sampled agent traces to establish gold datasets and audit automated judge alignment.
how_to_run: Export representative production and eval trajectories without model labels, collect blind expert scores, and measure agreement.
strengths: Provides authoritative ground truth across subjective legal, clinical, editorial, and UX quality dimensions.
limitations: Slow and costly to run continuously, restricting routine application to periodic calibration cohorts.

name: Long-Term Conversational Memory Recall Evaluation
what_it_measures: Evaluating whether memory-augmented agents retrieve and apply facts introduced across distant past sessions accurately.
how_to_run: Run long multi-session conversation timelines followed by recall, temporal ordering, and adversarial contradiction probes.
strengths: Tests episodic memory decay, write-back conflict resolution, and semantic consolidation directly.
limitations: Long interaction histories require careful fixture construction to mirror messy real enterprise usage.

name: Holistic Multi-Dimension Evaluation (HELM)
what_it_measures: Evaluating language systems concurrently across accuracy, calibration, robustness, fairness, toxicity, bias, and efficiency rather than single scores.
how_to_run: Define core target scenarios paired with standardized perturbations and multi-metric reporting tables per evaluated model.
strengths: Prevents narrow accuracy tuning from hiding serious robustness failures, calibration drift, or cost regressions.
limitations: Broad multi-metric evaluation matrices require significant compute sweeps per model family.

name: SWE-bench
what_it_measures: Real-world software engineering benchmark measuring whether coding agents resolve verified open-source GitHub repository issues.
how_to_run: Provide codebase checkout and issue description inside Dockerized sandboxes, run the agent patch, and verify hidden repository unit tests.
strengths: Tests authentic multi-file repository navigation, bug localization, test editing, and patch correctness cleanly.
limitations: Concentrates heavily on Python open-source repositories and bugfixes rather than full system greenfield design.

name: GAIA General AI Assistants Benchmark
what_it_measures: Evaluation benchmark testing generalist assistants across realistic multi-step tasks combining reasoning, multimodal reading, browsing, and tool use.
how_to_run: Run evaluated assistants against tiered real-world question suites verified via strict unambiguous exact ground-truth answers.
strengths: Resistant to naive shortcut memorization because solutions demand live synthesis across multi-hop web and file evidence.
limitations: Unambiguous exact-match targets cover closed-ended factual questions better than open-ended creative drafting.

name: OSWorld
what_it_measures: Real computer environment benchmark assessing multimodal agents across Ubuntu and Windows desktop applications, browsers, shells, and office tools.
how_to_run: Launch live virtual machine task images, expose pixel screens and accessibility trees cleanly, and run automated post-task state scripts.
strengths: Measures genuine end-to-end GUI, mouse, keyboard, and multi-application computer use without artificial mocks.
limitations: VM orchestration infrastructure demands substantial compute and careful timing tolerances on asynchronous UI renders.

name: tau-bench (Tool-Agent-User Benchmark)
what_it_measures: Interactive domain benchmark testing conversational customer-service agents over dynamic APIs, database rules, and simulated human users.
how_to_run: Execute multi-turn tool and user simulation episodes in retail and airline sandboxes while verifying final DB consistency and consistency metrics.
strengths: Measures realistic policy obedience, edge-case clarification, and multi-trial stability rather than isolated text chat.
limitations: Currently centers around specific retail and airline policies needing customization for wider enterprise domains.

name: WebArena
what_it_measures: Self-hosted realistic web environment benchmark featuring functional e-commerce, forum, GitLab, and CMS apps for browser agents.
how_to_run: Deploy deterministic local Docker web replicas, let browser agents navigate live DOMs, and grade outcomes via URL and DB verification.
strengths: Reproducible self-hosted websites prevent external internet changes from breaking repeated agent comparisons.
limitations: Requires running local web application containers and misses some anti-bot quirks found on public sites.

name: AgentBench
what_it_measures: Multi-environment agent benchmark spanning operating systems, SQL databases, knowledge graphs, web interactions, and embodied reasoning tasks.
how_to_run: Connect candidate models via standardized environment containers and aggregate completion accuracy across eight interactive domains.
strengths: Surfaces cross-domain capability strengths vs instruction-following weaknesses cleanly within one suite.
limitations: Shorter turn horizons focus more on foundational loop execution than day-long autonomous projects.

name: Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard (BFCL)
what_it_measures: Tool-calling evaluation suite measuring syntactic schema validity, parameter typing, parallel invocation, irrelevance detection, and multi-turn execution.
how_to_run: Score AST parameter equality and live simulated function execution across diverse languages, REST schemas, and nested tool calls.
strengths: Clearly distinguishes models that follow complex parameter constraints from models that hallucinate missing tools.
limitations: Focused specifically on tool selection and schema formatting rather than long open-ended creative reasoning.

name: MT-Bench
what_it_measures: Multi-turn instruction-following benchmark assessing conversational coherence, reasoning, coding, and writing evaluated via LLM judges and human preferences.
how_to_run: Prompt models across structured two-turn dialogues spanning diverse capability categories and score responses with calibrated judges.
strengths: Established canonical empirical baseline showing high agreement between strong model judges and human crowd preferences.
limitations: Broad general chat tasks leave out autonomous multi-step tool loops and stateful enterprise environment interactions.

name: HumanEval
what_it_measures: Functional correctness benchmark assessing standalone Python function synthesis from docstrings against hidden unit-test assertions.
how_to_run: Generate candidate function completions and execute isolated unit test suites to compute functional pass rates.
strengths: Fast deterministic baseline verifying fundamental language-model code syntax and algorithmic reasoning accuracy.
limitations: Small self-contained puzzles do not capture multi-file repository comprehension, dependencies, or iterative debugging loops.

name: MMLU and BIG-Bench
what_it_measures: Broad multitask knowledge and capability benchmark suites covering STEM, humanities, professional domains, and tricky reasoning tasks.
how_to_run: Evaluate zero-shot and few-shot question accuracy across diverse subject distributions using standardized prompt formats.
strengths: Useful baseline sanity check tracking general parametric world knowledge and foundation-model scaling trends.
limitations: Static multiple-choice exams saturate easily and fail to test tool calling, memory, retrieval, or interactive planning.

name: Ragas Evaluation Framework
what_it_measures: Open-source Python evaluation toolkit providing reference-free RAG and agentic metrics spanning faithfulness, context recall, and tool checks.
how_to_run: Supply evaluation datasets of queries, retrieved contexts, tool traces, and answers to compute modular metric scores in CI or notebooks.
strengths: Eliminates manual boilerplate when scoring RAG fidelity and supports testset generation directly from corpora.
limitations: LLM-backed metrics depend heavily on carefully chosen evaluator models and clear domain rubrics.

name: DeepEval Unit-Testing Suite
what_it_measures: Pytest-integrated LLM evaluation framework for running conversational, RAG, hallucination, and agentic safety assertions inside developer workflows.
how_to_run: Author declarative test cases specifying metrics, thresholds, and custom G-Eval rubrics executed via standard Python test runners.
strengths: Integrates AI regression gates seamlessly alongside conventional software unit tests inside CI pull requests.
limitations: High metric counts require careful selection so teams track relevant failure modes rather than noisy boilerplate.

name: TruLens Feedback and Trace Evaluation
what_it_measures: Observability and feedback-function library built around OpenTelemetry spans and the RAG Triad evaluation workflow.
how_to_run: Instrument agent applications cleanly with TruLens wrappers and evaluate logged intermediate steps using pluggable feedback criteria.
strengths: Tightly couples trace observability with systematic feedback evaluation over retrieved chunks and inner agent spans.
limitations: Multi-framework tracing setup requires consistent span instrumentation across custom internal orchestrators.

name: OpenAI Evals and Braintrust Scoring Harnesses
what_it_measures: Hosted and SDK evaluation harnesses linking versioned test datasets, programmatic scorers, human review queues, and side-by-side prompt diffs.
how_to_run: Define structured eval datasets and scoring functions via SDK or UI, then execute sweeps comparing prompt and model revisions.
strengths: Streamlines collaborative debugging by tying dataset metrics directly to individual failing production traces.
limitations: Hosted scoring platforms require privacy governance when sensitive enterprise user traces leave private VPCs.

name: CI Prompt and Model Regression Gating
what_it_measures: Automated release workflow executing critical behavioral, schema, citation, and latency evals prior to merging prompt or model changes.
how_to_run: Trigger targeted eval slices in pull requests against mocked/deterministic harnesses and fail merges when safety or schema accuracy drops.
strengths: Catches silent cross-workflow side effects systematically before end users encounter broken agents.
limitations: Requires maintaining fast stable mocks and budget bounds so CI runs stay reliable and rapid.

name: Adversarial Red-Teaming and Canary Auditing
what_it_measures: Scheduled security probing paired with shadow/canary telemetry monitoring to catch emergent jailbreaks, drift, and real-world regressions.
how_to_run: Combine curated adversarial attack sweeps pre-release with gradual traffic rollouts tracking safety alerts, refusals, and fallback spikes.
strengths: Bridges the gap between clean synthetic benchmarks and messy adversarial production reality.
limitations: Continuous human triage of canary anomalies demands disciplined operational ownership and alert thresholds.
